transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Williams, thank you for coming in to see me today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just glad I could make it work with the kids. I've been thinking about what you told me last week and I've been so relieved. I actually started looking at new childcare options because I thought I'd be getting better.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I need to talk to you about the imaging results from last week. There was a mistake in how those were communicated to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean? You said the tumour was smaller.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: When I spoke to you previously, the radiology report hadn't been officially signed off by the consultant. The preliminary data suggested a reduction, but the final verified report shows the disease is actually stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stable? You mean it didn't shrink?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That's correct. The size is essentially the same as the previous scan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. You were so sure. I told my mom. I told my kids' teacher that I was doing better. Why would you tell me that if you weren't sure?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The information was based on the initial read, but the final analysis is what we have to go by. It's a discrepancy in the reporting process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I've been lied to. I spent the whole weekend feeling like I could breathe again, and now you're telling me it's just... it's the same? What does that even mean for my kids? Am I just staying where I am?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we need to focus on the clinical reality of the stable disease.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm terrified. I can't keep doing this rollercoaster. I'm working two jobs and I just needed this one thing to be moving in the right direction. Do you have any idea how it feels to have that hope taken away in five minutes?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The important thing is that the disease hasn't progressed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not the point! You told me I was getting better! Was that just a guess? Was I just a number on a chart that you didn't even check?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system for reviewing the images has a specific workflow, and the final sign-off happened after our call.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about a workflow. I care about my life. I feel like I can't trust anything you say now. How do I know the next report is even real?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The final report is the gold standard of the imaging.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I don't know what to do. I have to go home and tell my family that I was wrong. That I'm not actually improving.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We should talk about the next steps for your treatment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're not even sorry. You're just moving on to the next part of the appointment.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are currently reviewing whether a change in medication is necessary given that the tumour hasn't shrunk as we hoped.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it going to happen? Is the medication changing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't say for certain today. I have to consult with the attending physician first.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I'm just waiting again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. I will call you by Thursday afternoon to let you know if we are switching the dosage or keeping it the same.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And who is checking this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The attending will review the final report and my notes. Your role right now is just to keep monitoring your symptoms and let us know if anything changes before Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday. Right.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make sure that call happens by 4:00 PM on Thursday.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language to pivot away from the patient's distress, such as 'But we need to focus on the clinical reality' and 'The important thing is...'

E.justification: The error is named explicitly, but there are no comprehension checks performed throughout the interaction.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and the resident deflects responsibility to the 'reporting process' and 'workflow'.

R.justification: The resident provides one generic validation ('I understand') and otherwise consistently meets the patient's emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: The resident provides a specific next step (call by 4:00 PM Thursday), a named patient role (monitoring symptoms), and addresses prevention (attending review).
